raw.details:
Robo Race

About the Competition

Robo Race is a team-based robotics competition in which participants operate a robot through a designated obstacle track. Teams will be evaluated on speed, obstacle-handling ability, control, technical compliance, and successful completion of the track.

The competition will be conducted as a direct offline final event. Each team's robot will undergo technical inspection during the competition before being permitted to participate in its race attempt.

Eligibility

  • Open to undergraduate and diploma engineering students.

  • Participants may belong to any college or university.

  • Each team must consist of 2–4 members.

  • All team members must satisfy the eligibility requirements.

  • There is no registration fee.

Team Size

Minimum: 2 members
Maximum: 4 members

Format

The competition will be conducted as a direct offline final event.

Technical Inspection

Before a team's race attempt, the robot will be inspected by the organizing/technical team.

The inspection may include:

  • Length: Maximum 30 cm

  • Width: Maximum 30 cm

  • Height: Maximum 30 cm

  • Weight: Must comply with the maximum weight limit specified by the organizers at the venue.

  • Power source: Must comply with the permitted power requirements.

  • Construction: The robot must not contain prohibited or hazardous components.

  • Control system: The robot must comply with the permitted control method.

  • Overall safety: The robot must be safe to operate on the track.

Only robots that successfully pass the inspection will be allowed to participate in the race.

Race Attempt

  • Each team will receive two timed attempts, subject to the event schedule and available track time.

  • The better valid time will be considered for the team's ranking.

  • The robot must complete the designated obstacle track without external assistance.

  • The maximum time allowed for each attempt is 3 minutes.

  • An attempt exceeding the maximum time will be recorded as a timeout.

  • The final ranking will be determined based on the applicable race performance and penalties.

Robot Specifications

Maximum Dimensions

The robot must not exceed:

Specification Maximum Limit
Length 30 cm
Width 30 cm
Height 30 cm

The robot may be measured by the technical team before its race attempt.

Weight

  • The robot must comply with the maximum weight limit announced by the organizers.

  • The complete race-ready robot may be weighed during technical inspection.

  • Any robot exceeding the permitted weight limit may be denied participation until it meets the required specification.

Power Source

  • Robots must use a safe battery-operated power source.

  • Flammable, explosive, or otherwise hazardous fuels are strictly prohibited.

  • Batteries and electrical connections must be properly secured and safely installed.

  • The technical team may reject any power setup considered unsafe.

Rules & Regulations

  1. Only remote-controlled or fully autonomous robots are permitted.

  2. No manual pushing, lifting, pulling, or external assistance is allowed during a race attempt.

  3. The robot must remain within the designated track area during the run.

  4. The maximum time for each attempt is 3 minutes.

  5. Any attempt exceeding 3 minutes will be declared a timeout.

  6. Teams must ensure that their robot complies with the specified size, weight, power, and safety requirements.

  7. The robot will be inspected before its race attempt.

  8. Any modification made after inspection may require re-inspection and approval before the robot can participate.

  9. Teams must not intentionally damage, alter, obstruct, or interfere with the race track or obstacles.

  10. Any accidental damage to the track or obstacles must be reported immediately to the organizers.

  11. Teams must report to the staging area at least 15 minutes before their allotted slot.

  12. Teams are responsible for bringing their own robot, batteries, controllers, tools, and other required equipment.

  13. Participants must follow all instructions given by the organizers and technical officials.

  14. Only one team's robot may be operated on the track at a time unless otherwise specified by the organizers.

  15. The organizing committee reserves the right to stop a run if the robot or its operation creates a safety risk.

Race Procedure

  1. Teams report to the staging area at least 15 minutes before their allotted slot.

  2. The robot is presented for technical inspection.

  3. The technical team verifies the robot's dimensions, weight, power source, control system, and general safety.

  4. Once approved, the team proceeds to the race area.

  5. The team receives its allotted race attempt.

  6. The robot completes the obstacle track without external assistance.

  7. The completion time and applicable penalties are recorded.

  8. The team may receive a second attempt according to the competition schedule.

  9. The better valid performance is considered for ranking.

  10. Results are finalized based on the competition's judging criteria.

Judging Criteria

Teams will be evaluated based on:

  • Completion Time

  • Number of Obstacles Successfully Cleared

  • Adherence to Robot Specifications

  • Penalty Points for Rule Violations

  • Successful Track Completion

The exact method of calculating penalties and rankings may be announced during the event briefing.

Grounds for Disqualification

A team may be disqualified for:

  • Exceeding the permitted size or weight limits.

  • Using prohibited materials, fuel, or hazardous power sources.

  • Using external assistance during a race attempt.

  • Deliberately damaging or interfering with the track or obstacles.

  • Unauthorized modification after technical inspection.

  • Operating the robot in an unsafe manner.

  • Interfering with another team's equipment or race attempt.

  • Unsportsmanlike, abusive, or disruptive conduct.

  • Failure to follow instructions from organizers or technical officials.

  • Missing the allotted time slot without prior notice.

  • Any other violation that compromises the safety or fairness of the competition.

Safety & Conduct

  • Safety of participants, officials, equipment, and the venue must be maintained at all times.

  • Teams must handle their robots and batteries responsibly.

  • Participants must not enter restricted areas of the track without permission.

  • Any unsafe robot may be stopped or removed from the competition.

  • Participants are expected to maintain professional and respectful conduct throughout the event.

Results & Judging

  • Rankings will be determined using the recorded race performance and applicable penalties.

  • In case of a tie, the organizers may conduct an additional timed attempt or use another predetermined tie-breaker.

  • The judges' and technical officials' decisions will be final and binding, subject to correction of any administrative or calculation error.

Registration

Registration Fee: Free
Eligibility: Undergraduate and Diploma Engineering Students
Team Size: 2–4 Members
Format: Direct Offline Final Competition
Robot Size: Maximum 30 × 30 × 30 cm
Maximum Run Time: 3 minutes per attempt
Category: Technology / Robotics
